mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% and remains above for at least two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% month-over-month triggers a demand pullback mechanism that depresses earnings expectations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST m/m change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer purchasing power and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at the 5% confidence level.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% during a period when the unemployment rate is below 4% indicates a supply-side shock in a tight labor market, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with supply disruption
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate below 2% during a period of negative GDP growth (proxied by GDPC1 decline) signals an aggressive easing cycle, which lowers risk-free rates and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls below 2% AND GDPC1 shows two consecutive quarterly declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes at the 5% confidence level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth above 0.5% for four consecutive months) without a corresponding rise in consumer spending (GDPC1 flat) indicates a savings glut, which reduces near-term consumption demand and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS m/m change > 0.5% for four consecutive months AND GDPC1 m/m change ≈ 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in these episodes at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for six consecutive months, irrespective of other macro conditions, consistently precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to broad-based earnings contraction.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for six consecutive months at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month surge in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1.5% during a period of stable unemployment (UNRATE change within ±0.2%) signals a supply-side expansion without labor market overheating, which boosts corporate earnings and yields positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO m/m change > 1.5% AND |UNRATE m/m change| ≤ 0.2%
regime_hint: supply-side expansion in stable labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes at the 5% confidence level.
